name: leads-out-of-area
about: Earlier ads drew many leads from too far away; the plan should say where the job is.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 40 were called and 27 were reached.
19 of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days were closed as: out of area.
4 of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days were closed as: not interested.

output.audience: Class A flatbed drivers who meet the experience requirement and live along the Midwest lanes. They likely run for a larger carrier now and want home weekly, an assigned truck and a dispatcher who knows them. A plainly stated area and pay per mile would make them stop.

angles.idea: Say plainly who this is for: Class A drivers with the required experience who live near the Midwest lanes.
angles.proof: The opening is Class A regional, states an experience requirement and runs Midwest lanes.
angles.why: The largest share of closed leads were out of area. An ad that states the area and the requirement up front should bring fewer wasted calls.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, and name flatbed and Midwest lanes in the same line.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile, on flatbed, on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Pay is the firmest fact of the job. Naming the lanes beside it helps screen the out-of-area leads the earlier ads drew.

angles.idea: Lead with home weekly, and say the freight runs Midwest lanes.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly and runs Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Home time is what a regional driver weighs against pay. No ad result by hook has been measured yet, so this is an early test.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck, shown parked with its flatbed trailer.
angles.proof: The job details list an assigned truck and flatbed work.
angles.why: Flatbed drivers care about their equipment and about not sharing it. The picture also shows the trailer type, so drivers who do not want flatbed pass by.

angles.idea: Set the job's facts out as a plain list: pay per mile, home weekly, retirement plan, small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.proof: Each line is a stated fact of the opening, and the small-fleet line is the carrier's own description.
angles.why: A driver who sees every term before applying is less likely to close as not interested. That closure count is small, so treat this as a test.
